newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela admits S.Africa's ruling ANC made mistakes.
newsitem.headline: Mandela admits S.Africa's ruling ANC made mistakes.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela admitted on Sunday that his ruling African National Congress had made major mistakes in its nearly three years in power.

"We have of course made mistakes. Some of them very fundamental and serious," Mandela told several thousand people gathered to mark the 1912 founding of the ANC, South Africa's oldest political movement.

Among the errors he listed were a multi-million rand (dollar) musical intended to educate people about AIDS, which was scrapped as hugely wasteful, and a scandal which surrounded secret funds donated by businessmen to the party.

"The question is not so much whether one makes mistakes or not but rather whether...we are prepared to admit our mistakes and above all, to learn from and quickly rectify weaknesses in our work," he told the crowds gathered at a stadium near Bloemfontein in the central Free State province.
Mandela said progress was being made despite the problems which confronted the ANC since it took power in South Africa's first all-race elections in April 1994.
Schools, clinics and sanitation had improved in many areas, he said, adding: "Even on the housing front, where progress has been slow...construction is now starting to come on stream.
"We are not always moving as fast as we would like. We have reverses and make mistakes, but everywhere there is now visible evidence of a new South Africa in the making."
He said massive projects in various parts of the country were central to the economic development of South Africa and its neighbours.
Mandela said 1997 would be a crucial year for the ANC, which holds a large parliamentary majority and massive support among South Africans.
He is due to step down as party leader at a congress in December, but will continue in office as South Africa's president until the country's second all-race elections are held in 1999.
His party deputy, Thabo Mbeki, is widely expected to take over the reins when Mandela steps down.
